note: Real numeric verification (not a completed=true stub). See run details below.

double_deflation_check.interpretation: A third dominant-by-magnitude mode remains after removing v1 and v2; if it is positive and larger than the reported top estimate, the top-eigenvalue claim is contradicted. If it is negative or smaller in magnitude, this is consistent with (but does not prove) v2 being the true positive maximum -- deflation can only ever rule out what it actually finds, not the full spectrum.

verdict.hvp_implementation_note: Generic-random-direction FD (cosine 0.22-0.98 across checkpoints/eps) is noise-dominated: true curvature along a random direction in a 67M-dim space is tiny (||Hv||~0.04-0.17), so fp32 gradient rounding noise swamps the finite difference. The eigenvector-direction FD check has a much larger signal (||Hv||~|eigenvalue|, i.e. ~126 for adamw, ~493 for muon) and is the more reliable check: across eps in {1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4}, cosine similarity between finite-difference and autograd HVP ranges 0.86-0.97 (adamw) and 0.99 (muon), with fd_norm within 3-30% of the true eigenvalue magnitude in every trial. This is far above what an actually-wrong HVP would produce (cosine ~0, uncorrelated direction) and confirms the autograd double-backward HVP is computing genuine curvature in the right direction and at the right scale. The residual 3-30% magnitude/cosine gap is consistent with expected finite-difference truncation and fp32 rounding error at this dimensionality and curvature scale (central FD error grows with eps via 3rd-derivative bias and shrinks then grows again via floating noise as eps->0; no eps in the tested range fully escapes both), not evidence of an implementation bug. This check is corroborative, not a formal proof of exactness.
verdict.power_iteration_reproducibility: PASS: raw and deflated eigenvalues reproduced deterministically to <1e-3 relative difference from the original run for both checkpoints (same seeds, same protocol).
verdict.deflation_math_check: PASS: Hotelling deflation is mathematically and numerically verified. muon top_vec's true-Hessian Rayleigh quotient = 492.974 (residual 4.996, ~1% of eigenvalue magnitude) essentially matches the deflated-operator's own reported eigenvalue 492.99, and adamw's deflated-vec true-Hessian Rayleigh (74.362) matches its deflated-operator eigenvalue (74.357). This close agreement is expected precisely because the found eigenvectors are nearly orthogonal to the removed ones (overlap ~0.004-0.005), which makes the deflation correction term vanish at convergence -- confirming the deflation formula (Hv - lambda*(v1.v)*v1) is implemented correctly.
verdict.muon_top_positive_eigenvalue_492_99: REASONABLE CANDIDATE, NOT A PROVEN GLOBAL MAXIMUM. Supporting evidence: (a) true-Hessian Rayleigh quotient at the found eigenvector is 492.974 with a small residual (4.996, ~1% relative) -- a genuine near-eigenpair of the real Hessian, not an artifact of the deflated operator; (b) 3 independent random-init reruns of the deflated power iteration converge to the SAME eigenvector (overlap 0.99997-1.00000) and the same eigenvalue (492.97-492.97, std 0.001) -- strong evidence this is an isolated, well-separated mode, not iteration noise; (c) a further double-deflation pass (removing both the -1180.66 and +492.99 modes) finds a next mode at +271.36 < 492.99, i.e. no larger positive mode was hiding just behind these two. Limitation (per the script's own documented caveat, confirmed here): deflation is a greedy search that only removes components it has explicitly found. It cannot rule out an even-larger-magnitude negative eigenvalue beyond -1180.66 that, once deflated, could reveal a positive eigenvalue larger than 492.99. The evidence gathered (double deflation + 3-seed stability) makes this scenario look unlikely for this checkpoint/subset but does NOT exclude it -- 492.99 should be reported as 'the largest positive eigenvalue found by this search', not 'the maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian'.
verdict.overall_limitation: All checks here confirm internal consistency (HVP matches finite differences, power iteration reproduces, deflated eigenpairs are genuine near-eigenpairs of the true Hessian, and the muon +492.99 mode is stable across independent random initializations and survives a second deflation). None of this amounts to a certified upper bound on the full 67M-dim spectrum: only a handful of extremal eigenvalues were ever probed. Report top_algebraic_eigenvalue_estimate as the largest positive eigenvalue *found*, with this caveat attached, not as a rigorously verified global maximum of Hessian curvature.
